data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root ‘n-f-h’ meaning to be sufficient or enough. In Islamic tradition, Nafih is a name that evokes feelings of contentment and satisfaction with the blessings of Allah. The name Nafih carries the meaning “Satisfied, content, sufficing” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Nafih usually hope their child will grow to embody satisfied, content, sufficing and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Nafih ibn al-Mundhir was a prominent companion of the Prophet Muhammad and a member of the Ansar of Medina. He was a skilled horseman and a fierce warrior, and played a significant role in the early battles of Islam. He was one of the first converts to Islam in Medina and was known for his generosity and hospitality.

Nafih ibn al-Harith al-Misri was a famous Sufi scholar and poet of the 9th century CE. He was born in Egypt and studied under many great Sufi masters, including Junayd al-Baghdadi and Abu al-Qasim al-Qushayri. His poetry explored the themes of love for God and the longing for union with the Divine, and he is considered a major figure in the development of Sufi literature.
